10-year yields have more or less recovered fully to be back up to 4.704% now while 30-year yields are nudging back up to 5.251% on the day.

However, whether or not yields will look to break higher will depend on the conviction of the bond vigilantes - whom might be still cautious in wanting to challenge the "Bessent put" so quickly.

After the Wednesday announcement to double long-term debt buybacks, Bessent stepped in with some verbal intervention of his own yesterday.

In case you missed it: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says the long-dated bond buyback could be more than $4 billion This all sounds rather familiar, doesn't it?

It's a sort of similar playbook to what the BOJ has been doing in trying to defend the yen currency.

As mentioned before, any Treasury intervention of sorts will still be a drop in the bucket against a massive Treasury market of over $30 trillion.

Hence, the move is very much meant to be a signaling effort - much like currency intervention.
